newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to meet prime minister on reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to meet prime minister on reshuffle.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin will meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin in the Kremlin at 1 p.m. (1000 GMT) on Thursday, the presidential press service said.
Interfax news agency said the two men would discuss the new line-up of the cabinet following Yeltsin's decision to reshuffle the government dramatically.
Yeltsin blasted the government for failing to tackle the economic and social crisis in Russia in his state of the nation address last Thursday and ordered Chernomyrdin to reorganise the cabinet.
He also made clear that Chernomyrdin and newly-appointed First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais would keep their posts in the new cabinet.

Chubais would be the only first deputy premier -- there are four now -- while the number of deputy premiers and ministers would be cut. He is a hate figure for conservatives for his role in kick-starting Russia's tough privatisation drive in 1992 and spearheading Yeltsin's successful re-election campaign last summer.
Chernomyrdin said on Wednesday the new cabinet, which he had promised to present later this week, would be younger and more professional and would include market-minded reformers.
